# `liber:power@1`

Generated reference for the `liber:power` package (`power.lsidl`). See [the LSIDL language](../../../LSIDL.md).

LiberSystem power state - what power sources and thermal zones report, normalised, and the few device controls an operator may use.  THREE INTERFACES FOR THREE PARTIES. A READER sees normalised state and nothing it could change; an OPERATOR may switch an advertised output of a device such as a UPS; a PROVIDER - a driver - publishes what its hardware reports. None of them reaches the others' operations, because what separates them is who holds them.  THIS IS NOT MACHINE SHUTDOWN. Rebooting and powering off the host stay with SystemManager's `system-power`; this service holds no client of it. Turning a UPS's output off turns the UPS's output off. Suspend, fan curves and power policy are not here at all.

## Interfaces

### interface `power`

THE READ AUTHORITY: enumerate, and subscribe. No publication and no control.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `sources` | `sources() -> result<list<source-snapshot>, error>` | Every live source, sorted. Informational: a subscription is correct without it. |
| 2 | `subscribe` | `subscribe() -> result<stream<power-change>, error>` | One atomic snapshot at (epoch, revision), then live changes after it. REFUSED with `exhausted` at the service's subscriber limit, rather than admitted and starved. |

### interface `power-control`

THE OPERATOR AUTHORITY: device controls a provider advertises, and only those. Granted to one explicitly authorised administrative component and to nothing by default.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `set-output` | `set-output(source: source-id, outlet: u8, on: bool) -> result<control-outcome, error>` |  |
| 2 | `schedule-output-off` | `schedule-output-off(source: source-id, delay-seconds: u32) -> result<control-outcome, error>` |  |
| 3 | `cancel-output-off` | `cancel-output-off(source: source-id) -> result<control-outcome, error>` |  |

### interface `power-provider`

THE PROVIDER CONTRACT a `power-source` publication serves - to PowerService alone.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `updates` | `updates() -> stream<provider-update>` |  |
| 2 | `command` | `command(command: provider-command) -> result<control-outcome, error>` |  |
| 3 | `query` | `query(local: u32) -> result<source-state, error>` | A fresh state of one source, for reconciliation after an indeterminate command. |

### interface `power-fixture`

THE FIXTURE'S CONTROL ENDPOINT: change or remove what the two fixture providers publish, make one withhold its replies, and read back every command they were sent and what their outlets are.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `set` | `set(field: fixture-field, value: u32) -> result<unit, error>` |  |
| 2 | `remove` | `remove(publication: u8, local: u32) -> result<unit, error>` | Remove one source from a publication. |
| 3 | `withdraw` | `withdraw(publication: u8) -> result<unit, error>` | Withdraw a whole publication, as a device going would. |
| 4 | `republish` | `republish(publication: u8) -> result<unit, error>` | Publish a withdrawn one again: a new publication, so a new generation and new sources. |
| 5 | `commands` | `commands() -> result<list<fixture-command>, error>` |  |
| 6 | `withhold` | `withhold(commands: u32, queries: u32) -> result<unit, error>` | Leave the next `commands` control replies and `queries` reconciliation replies unanswered. |
| 7 | `offer-extra` | `offer-extra() -> result<unit, error>` | Offer one more `power-source` publication than this fixture's registry entry declares, which DeviceManager must refuse. |
| 8 | `outlets` | `outlets() -> result<list<bool>, error>` | The UPS's outlets, on or off, in order. |
